patch.value: Retrieval quality contract: measured recall and precision targets for pm search across corpus scales, gated in CI like latency already is

Search latency is benchmarked at 10k, 100k, and a million items, but search quality is not measured at all: nothing states what fraction of relevant items a query should return, nothing detects a ranking regression, and the hybrid weighting was chosen by decision rather than by measurement. Context relevance has an evaluation harness owned separately; search has none, even though search is what an agent reaches for first when it does not know an identifier. This feature defines a retrieval quality contract - a labelled query set over real and synthetic corpora, declared recall and precision targets per corpus scale, and a CI gate that fails on regression - and makes the hybrid weighting an evidence-backed parameter rather than a fixed constant. The judgment corpus deliberately reuses the shapes the context harness already defines, so the two evaluations report on one methodology instead of two.

A labelled query and relevance-judgment set exists over the real corpus and over generated corpora at multiple scales, reusing the context harness scenario shapes rather than defining a parallel methodology; Recall and precision targets are declared per corpus scale and per query class (identifier, exact phrase, conceptual, cross-lingual-free), and are measured by a repeatable command; CI fails when measured quality regresses below the declared targets, in the same way the latency gate fails on regression; The hybrid weighting is tuned against the judgment set and the chosen value is recorded with its measurement, superseding the constant chosen by decision alone; Results are published in a form the public benchmark can consume, so external claims and internal gates share one number
Retrieval quality is a measured, gated number rather than an assumption

An agent that cannot find an existing item files a duplicate. Search quality is therefore a direct input to backlog integrity, and it is currently the only hot path with no quality measurement at all.
Gives search the same regression protection latency already has, makes the hybrid weighting evidence-based, and supplies the retrieval half of the public context benchmark.
Declared recall and precision targets per scale, a repeatable measurement, and a CI gate that fails on ranking regression.
The search capability epic has no other open work, the scale corpus generator exists, and the duplicate-advisory work makes search quality a governance dependency rather than a nicety.

value.text:
Live measurement of the shipped eval command, build 2026.7.29, real corpus.

The retrieval side of this contract now has a command. It does not yet have a gate, a target, or a judgment set that can fail.

Measured: golden set is 4 queries in 694 bytes at .agents/pm/search/eval-queries.json (tracked in git since GH-807 closed). Aggregate at k=10: nDCG 0.7168, MRR 0.625, precision 0.125, recall 1.0. Recall is saturated because every query declares exactly one relevant item and the command retrieves ten, so precision is pinned at 0.1 per query by construction and no ranking regression short of dropping the single relevant item can move the aggregate. Query modes exercised: keyword only by default.

Wiring: the command's own help says to use --fail-under as a CI gate. It appears in zero of the 58 package.json scripts and zero of the six workflow files. The only wired relevance gate is scripts/release/context-eval-gate.mjs, invoked as quality:context-eval from ci.yml:231, release.yml:110 and scripts/release/run-gates.mjs:88 - it scores tests/context-eval/golden-scenarios.json, a different corpus, and never reads the eval query set.

Consequence for this item's criteria: the per-query-class targets (identifier, exact phrase, conceptual) are not yet expressible against a 4-query set, and the multi-scale requirement is blocked on shape-capable corpus generation, now tracked as pm-vv2lti. Gate wiring is now tracked as pm-b2hc4x and recorded here as a blocker.
